entries.title: ABaC:us — Austrian Baroque Corpus
entries.institution: Austrian Academy of Sciences (ÖAW), Austrian Centre for Digital Humanities and Cultural Heritage (ACDH-CH)
entries.notes: Digital corpus of German baroque literary texts (c. 1650-1750), focused on devotional literature around death preparation (Ars moriendi, Totentanz, Memento mori) connected with Abraham a Sancta Clara (1644-1709), e.g. Mercks Wienn (1680), Grosse Todten Bruderschaft (1681). First-edition principle, XML-TEI P5 with linguistic annotation (tokenisation, PoS tagging, lemmatisation) and person/place indices. Project directed by Claudia Resch and Ulrike Czeitschner; online since 2015, new infrastructure launched 2025. Project archive page: https://www.oeaw.ac.at/acdh/research/literary-studies/research/project-archive/abacus. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the RQ Open Corpus snapshot v2026.06 (in-core, deduplicated texts).

entries.title: Amadis in Translation (Digital Amadis)
entries.institution: University of Pittsburgh at Greensburg (Stacey Triplette, Elisa Beshero-Bondar) and Universidade de Santiago de Compostela (Helena Bermúdez Sabel)
entries.notes: Digital study of the transformation of Montalvo's Amadís de Gaula across editions and translations (Spanish, French, English, from the 1500s to the early 1800s). The corpus files are the 35 TEI XML chapters of the 1547 Sevilla printing of Montalvo's Amadís (facsimile source: Biblioteca Virtual de Andalucía), used to align Garci Rodríguez de Montalvo's text with Robert Southey's 1803 translation and study translation shifts. Project team: Stacey Triplette, Elisa Beshero-Bondar, Helena Bermúdez Sabel; maintained by Beshero-Bondar since 2015. Code and TEI data: https://github.com/ebeshero/Amadis-in-Translation (AGPL-3.0); archive DOI: https://doi.org/10.5281/zenodo.10892444. Project documentation and a 1533 frontispiece facsimile on the project site. entries.title: SERMO - Corpus de sermons protestants 1550-1750
entries.notes: SERMO is an SNSF project (2015-2018) at Neuchatel that produced an annotated corpus of 62 French Protestant sermons (~600k tokens, mostly printed in Geneva, by Calvin, Beze, Daille, Mestrezat, the Turrettini etc.), with tokenisation, lemmatisation and POS annotation for diachronic French linguistics. The XML corpus version 1 was released on Zenodo (DOI 10.5281/zenodo.14620210, CC BY 4.0); the project site (sermo.unine.ch) is live but the project itself closed in 2018. Corpus statistics (text, word and language counts, period) derived from the RQ Open Corpus snapshot v2026.06 (in-core, deduplicated texts).
